howDoI.q: How do I make a stall that sells something for coins?
How do I make a block that does nothing until the player has enough coins?
How do I make coins the player can spend?
How do I make coins left over come to the next level?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Spend It is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Up and Down climb a ladder. F2 shows your Money. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

This one is about spending. For points, see Coins and Score. For a door with a price, see Stronger Keys. For showing a count as pictures, see Show the Count.

pages.head: Level 1: A Key For 3 Coins
pages.html:
Level 1: A Key For 3 Coins

Two coins lie on the ground and a stall stands ahead. Its card says 3. Walk into it with two coins and nothing happens. Climb the ladder for two more, come back, and walk into it again: it takes three coins, the counter turns to SOLD, and a gold key is yours. One coin is left. The gold door farther on takes the key.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The coins. Open spendit.bbl in the blocks editor and pick the cash block. On its Touch tab, Effect counter is 3 and Effect amount is 1. Counter 3 is Game-Maker's own Money counter. It has no score, because this is spending, not points.
  • The price. The stall block (stall.key.3) has the same Effect counter, 3, with an Effect amount of −3. That is the whole price tag.
  • Too few. A counter holds one more than the coins carried, and a touch is only allowed if the counter stays above zero. With two coins the counter holds 3, and 3 − 3 is not above zero, so the stall does nothing. With three coins it holds 4, and the stall takes three.
  • The key. A block has only one Effect counter, and the price uses it. So the stall turns into another block when it is paid (set on the same Touch tab): give.key. It is passable. Step into it and it adds 1 to counter 20, the key counter, then turns into sold, the empty counter with a SOLD card.
  • The picture of the price. The roof (awning3) is an ordinary passable block with a coin and a 3 drawn on a card. The picture says the price; the rule on the stall block takes it. Keep the two the same by hand.
  • Money. Open hero.chr in the character editor. Counter 3 starts at 1, which the game shows as none. Press F2 while you play to see Money: 0 and the number as you gather coins.
  • The door. The gold gate takes one key from counter 20 and then lets you through.

pages.head: Level 2: Save Up
pages.html:
Level 2: Save Up

The stall now wants five coins, and there are exactly five in the level: three on the ground and two up the ladder. The coin left over from level 1 stays in your pocket, so you leave with one. Buy the key, open the gold door, and go.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A new price. stall.key.5 is a copy of the first stall with its Effect amount changed to −5, and its roof (awning5) redrawn with a 5. Both stalls turn into the same give.key.
  • Money carries. Counters are not reset when a level ends. The coin left in level 1 is still counter 3 here. Nothing in this level mentions it.
  • Enough coins. Level 2 has five coins, the price. So a player who spent every coin in level 1 can still buy the key here. Check your own levels for the same: each one should have as many coins as it needs.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

  • There is no number on the screen while you play. Money is a counter, and Game-Maker prints only one counter as a number: Money, counter 3, on the status page (F2). The change you get back is on that page and nowhere else. The price is in the picture, which you draw yourself.
  • A block has one Effect counter. The price uses it, so the item has to come from the block the stall turns into. A stall can sell one thing; two items for one price means two stalls.
  • A price is the same every time. There is no haggling, no sale price and no change that depends on the item.
  • The picture and the price are separate. Change stall.key.3's Effect amount and the card on the roof still says 3 until you redraw it.
  • Money is counter 3 for everything. Two kinds of money would need two counters from 20 up, which the status page does not print.
  • A bought item cannot be taken back. Once the stall is sold, it stays sold until you play the level again.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In spendit.bbl, change stall.key.3's Effect amount to −2. Now two coins buy the key, though the card still says 3.
  • Change cash's Effect amount to 2. Each coin is worth two.
  • Copy give.key, set its Effect counter to 1 and make it a heart, and the stall sells a life. (Yana's Shop does this.)
  • Take a coin out of level 2's map. The key can no longer be bought there. Put it back.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.back: A small explorer in a pink beanie gathers coins and visits a stall. A key costs three, and with two the stall does nothing. Pay, and it takes three and keeps the rest of your Money for later. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and change a price.

A stall sells a key and says SOLD
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Two short levels about spending. Coins add to your Money, and a stall sells a gold key for a price: touch it with enough coins and it takes them and hands over the key. With too few, nothing happens. Money carries to the next level, and the Money counter is the one Game-Maker prints as a number (F2). Signs in the levels say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and change a price.
